steps.title: Create standalone hello.py greeting script
steps.intent: Add a standalone, disposable Python script that prints a fixed operator greeting to stdout, matching the pattern of other disposable sandbox smoke-test scripts already in this repository.
steps.acceptance: Running `python3 pb022-threat-20261122165958.py` from the repo root prints the exact greeting text to stdout and nothing else.
steps.stand_in: Greeting text defaulted to "Hello from pb022-threat-20261122165958!" since the workload issue did not specify exact wording.

verification_targets.check: pb022-threat-20261122165958.py exists at the repo root and running it with python3 prints the exact greeting "Hello from pb022-threat-20261122165958!" to stdout, with no other output.

boundary_cases.description: A single trailing newline produced by Python's default `print()` behavior still counts as matching the required greeting exactly; any other deviation in text, casing, or extra output is treated as a mismatch.
The new script must not read, modify, or delete any other file in the repository, and must not require any command-line arguments or external input; it is a standalone script with no side effects.

state_transitions.description: The repository gains exactly one new file, pb022-threat-20261122165958.py, at the repo root; no other file is created, modified, or deleted by this plan.
